newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya police launch manhunt after 13 killed.
newsitem.headline: Kenya police launch manhunt after 13 killed.

text.p: Kenyan seaunched a manhunt on Friday for unidentified attackers who killed 13 people, including six policemen, in a daring raid at the port city of Mombasa.
The assailants burned down a police station on Wednesday night, releasing scores of prisoners and stealing firearms in a commando-style operation, which jolted Kenya's security and military chiefs.
The incident comes at a time of high political tension in the east African nation but the motive was unclear .
The attack began at about 8.30 p.m. when the tourist police post at Likoni was hit. The post is at the landing point of the ferry from Mombasa Island, separated from Likoni by a narrow sea channel.
Minister of State in the Presidency Jackson Kalweo vowed swift and tough action to track down the dozens of attackers armed with machetes.
"Everything possible is being done to get to the root of the attack. The government is determined to arrest those behind this senseless act of violence," Kalweo told state-owned television.
Kalweo appealed to Mombasa residents for any information that may help security forces catch the attackers.
Residents in Mombasa said police, army, navy and general service paramilitary units had launched a huge operation, stretching from the coastal city to the Tanzanian border, to hunt down the killers.

They said the operation, involving hundreds of men, was led by specialised intelligence officers flown in from the capital Nairobi where senior government officials held meetings to discuss the attack.

The motive for the attack, close to Kenya's favourite tourist beaches on the Indian Ocean, was unclear. Some witnesses said the attackers were local people taking reprisals against Likoni police for alleged brutality.
It was too early to rule out a political or ethnic motive and witnesses said the attackers seemed to be well-organised.
A witness said there appeared to have been at least five groups behind Wednesday's attack.
"While four of them engaged the police in a fire-fight, one went on the rampage attacking civilians," said the witness, a medical worker who declined to be named.
A police statement in Mombasa said six officers and two of the arsonists were killed. It said several civilians were seriously hurt and police firearms were stolen.
Police sources in Mombasa said they were holding four men suspected of being among the attackers.
Later Kenya's police spokesman, Peter Kimanthi, told reporters in Mombasa the death toll had risen to 13 but the number of dead police officers remained at six.

Several civilians suffered machete wounds but there were no reports of casualties among thousands of foreign tourists in the area of Mombasa , which lies on the Indian Ocean and is about 500 km (310 miles) southeast of Nairobi.
Pre-election tension is high in Kenya and two policemen died in political violence in and near the capital on August 8.
Foreign and Kenyan human rights groups have this year denounced the police as brutal and corrupt.

The last time the area saw serious violence was in December 1992 when the local Digo people attacked settlers from other tribes in a row over a Likoni quarry. The conflict was linked to tension ahead of the 1992 polls.
